entries.title: White Sox slugger Colson Montgomery finding his swing again out west
entries.summary: <p>WEST SACRAMENTO, Calif. — This isn’t the first time Colson Montgomery has gone west in search of consistency in his swing.</p><p>He found it in the desert last season, when Montgomery’s status as the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox" target="_blank" ><u>White Sox</u></a>’ shortstop of the future briefly seemed to be in jeopardy amid a flailing start at Triple-A.</p><p>The 24-year-old found it in West Sacramento during the Sox’ series opener against the Athletics, socking a double and a screaming infield single on a 2-4 night with two RBI. He followed up with a laser of a home run to kickstart the Sox’ offense on Saturday, but struck out with the bases loaded in the 11th inning of their walk-off loss. </p><p>That's the way it's been for the hot-and-cold Mongomery as he tries to find steady production after an uneven start to the 6-3 slugger’s sophomore campaign. </p><p>“In his pregame work, sometimes you watch him, and I'm like, ‘Man, this guy's going to have a great day today,’” manager Will Venable said. “Whether it materializes in the game or not, I think just the way that he's working has been great. He's somebody that puts so much work into it. That consistency of being himself and the best version of himself more consistently is right around the corner.”</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" > <div class="TweetUrl"> <blockquote class="twitter-tweet"><p lang="en" dir="ltr">One pitch is all Colson Montgomery needed 😮‍💨 <a href="https://t.co/7ULt8joiYT">pic.twitter.com/7ULt8joiYT</a></p>— Chicago White Sox (@whitesox) <a href="https://twitter.com/whitesox/status/2045598434577551800?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">April 18, 2026</a></blockquote> <script async src="https://platform.twitter.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script> </div> </div> </div></div><p>Montgomery's hitting .194/.310/.417 with nearly twice as many strikeouts (27) as hits (14) to go with eight walks. Not a pretty line, but there are plenty worse on a Sox roster that was at the bottom of the MLB barrel in OPS before an offensive awakening this weekend in California.</p><p>For his part, the zen Montgomery has kept an even keel.</p><p>“I always tell myself I’m one swing away, one at-bat away, one game away,” Montgomery said after a <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox/2026/04/12/tanner-murray-home-run-white-sox-royals-colson-montgomery" target="_blank" ><u>two-hit afternoon</u></a> last weekend in Kansas City. “I feel like that keeps me going in a good positive mindset and kind of ready for the next pitch and the next at-bat or whatever, and not really worried about the past or whatever happened the day before.”</p><p>Then it’s safe to say he’s not worried about where he was this time last year, when Montgomery was <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox/2025/05/13/colson-montgomery-white-sox-returns-charlotte" >scrambling so badly</a> that Sox brass yanked him from Charlotte’s lineup and sent him to the organization’s Arizona training complex to rediscover the swing that made the Holland, Indiana, native their 2021 first-round draft pick.</p><p>The drastic measure worked, with Montgomery rebounding in time for a July 4 debut and blasting 21 second-half homers with an .840 OPS.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a There have been really good spurts where I am swinging the bat well and I am able to affect the team's chances of winning.’ But to his credit, has not hit the panic button,” said Sox hitting director Ryan Fuller, who oversaw Montgomery’s 2025 desert sabbatical. “Same guy every day, ready to work, and when it is tougher, he wants to work even harder.</p><p>“We think about last year, too, where he was in April and May and you had a year to build and by the time it was July, August, September, that’s when you want to be playing your best baseball,” Fuller said while the Sox were getting swept at home by Tampa Bay. “Like all these guys, they’re struggling right now. We’re going to get it right, we’re going to make adjustments. He’s confident in the work we’re going to put in and it’s going to start to show up.”</p><p>Maybe it’ll start showing up elsewhere in a young lineup where 10 players have less than two years of experience apiece.</p><p>“They’re going through struggle, a lot of these guys, for the first time at the big-league level. That is totally normal,” Fuller said. “You look at any team over the course of 162, there’s going to be 20 or 30 games that everyone kind of goes cold at once and it’s a tough spell. We can reframe this as we’re getting ours out of the way in April. That’s going to set us up for really good lessons when we get into June, July, August, when it’s hotter, those dog days of summer.”</p>

entries.title: Victims identified in West Garfield Park shooting
entries.summary: <p>The three people who were fatally shot Friday in West Garfield Park have been identified.</p><p>Kenneth M. Bell Jr., 27; Lavell Lee, 36; Rickia Williams, 32; and another man, 35, were standing on a sidewalk about 4:45 p.m. in the 4000 block of West Maypole Avenue when a driver pulled up to them and at least two people got out of the car and fired shots, Chicago police and the Cook County medical examiner’s office said.</p><p>Lee was shot multiple times and pronounced dead at the scene. Bell suffered multiple gunshot wounds and was pronounced dead at Mount Sinai Hospital. Williams was struck in the head and pronounced dead at Stroger Hospital, officials said.</p><p>The other man, who has not been identified, was shot multiple times and was taken to Stroger Hospital, where he was listed in critical condition, police said.</p><p>Another man was also injured while running away from the gunfire, according to a police report obtained by the Sun-Times. He was not shot but he suffered a broken ankle and was taken to Humboldt Park Health Hospital in good condition.</p><p>After the shooting, police at the scene appeared to be focused on Gotcha Faded, a barbershop on Pulaski Road near that location. Officers went in and out of the storefront, and officers guarded the entrance.</p><p>The business could not be reached for comment Saturday, and attempts to reach friends and family of the victims were unsuccessful.</p><p>Officers later found the vehicle involved in the shooting had been set on fire, according to the police report.</p><p>Area Four Detectives are investigating.</p>

entries.title: Fire blow two-goal lead in second half, settle for tie with Cincinnati
entries.summary: <p>CINCINNATI — Tom Barlow and Evander Da Silva Ferreira — known simply as “Evander” — each scored for Cincinnati, but it was an own-goal by the Fire's Dje D’Avilla in the 86th minute that gave the hosts a 3-3 tie Saturday night.</p><p>Evander's free kick into the area was redirected into the net by D’Avilla, capping Cincinnati's rally from a 3-1 second-half deficit. The Fire (4-2-2), who had won three consecutive games, are unbeaten in four straight.</p><p>“I think there's two ways we can look at this game,“ Fire coach Gregg Berhalter said. “The first way is to say that the side is much improved from last year in terms of coming to a difficult atmosphere and having the ambition to control the game, to win the game and to play, to score goals. So, happy with that.</p><p>“But on the other side, the defending was not nearly good enough to win the game. And if it wasn't for us scoring three goals, we would have lost the game because defensively we were very poor tonight. And we have to learn from that. We have to improve that, and we have to have much more compactness, shape and pressure on the ball.”</p><p>Hugo Cuypers, who returned after missing three games with a head injury, scored twice, and Philip Zinckernagel added a goal and an assist. Chris Brady had eight saves and became the third Fire Homegrown player to play 100 matches for the team, starting each game (Mauricio Pineda and Brian Gutierrez are the other two).</p><p>Zinckernagel converted from the penalty spot in the fifth minute of first-half stoppage time to give the Fire a 2-1 lead. Cuypers opened the scoring in the 26th minute, and his goal in the 48th made it 3-1.</p><p>“Yeah, it's been a tough two weeks for me being out with a head injury, but I was just really, really happy to be back, and I felt good,“ said Cuypers, who has scored at least one goal in each of his last five games and has six goals overall. “Had a few good training days before the game.</p><p>“I think the team performance in the first half helped, the way we were able to combine and play offensively. Unfortunately, we dropped back in the second half. But overall, it was a positive comeback.”</p><p>Barlow, who signed as a free agent with Cincinnati in January after two seasons with the Fire, scored in the 42nd minute. Evander made a penalty kick in the 79th to it make 3-2.</p><p>Roman Celentano had three saves for Cincinnati (2-4-2).</p><p>The Fire's next game is Saturday at Soldier Field against Sporting KC (7:30 p.m., Apple TV, 890-AM).<br></p>

entries.title: Resurgent White Sox offense stacks up hits, but not when they need them in 7-6 walk-off loss to A's
entries.summary: <p>WEST SACRAMENTO, Calif. — A suddenly hot-hitting <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox" target="_blank" ><u>White Sox</u></a> squad racked up eight more hits but couldn't get one when they needed it most before getting walked off Saturday by the Athletics 7-6 in 11 innings.</p><p>The Sox squandered three bases-loaded opportunities while their bullpen escaped two such jams to keep them in the game after blowing an early five-run lead.</p><p>"Not a lot going on with runners in scoring position as we moved through that game," manager <b>Will Venable</b> said after his team stranded 14, one fewer than the A's. "Man, that was a hard-fought game on both sides."</p><p><b>Colson Montgomery</b> got the Sox on the board in the second inning with his <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox/2026/04/18/colson-montgomery-white-sox-homers" >fourth home run</a> of the season, and the Sox piled on Athletics starter <b>Luis Severino</b>. <b>Everson Pereira</b> blooped a double to right field and came around on <b>Reese McGuire</b>’s single, before Andrew Benintendi thwacked a three-run homer to make it 5-0.</p><p>The A's chipped away at Sox starter <b>Erick Fedde</b>, who gave up three runs on two hits and four walks with three strikeouts over 4 ⅔ innings.</p><p><b>Munetaka Murakami</b> slammed his second mammoth home run in as many days, this one a solo blast in the seventh, but <b>Nick Kurtz</b> tied it up with a no-doubt two-run bomb off <b>Jordan Leasure</b> in the bottom half of the inning.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" > <div class="TweetUrl"> <blockquote class="twitter-tweet"><p lang="et" dir="ltr">🚨MUNETAKA MURAKAMI HOME RUN🚨 <a href="https://t.co/6HkumpBoWa">pic.twitter.com/6HkumpBoWa</a></p>— Chicago White Sox (@whitesox) <a href="https://twitter.com/whitesox/status/2045624564739150314?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">April 18, 2026</a></blockquote> <script async src="https://platform.twitter.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script> </div> </div> </div></div><p>A's third baseman <b>Max Muncy</b> eked out the game-winning sacrifice fly off Sox reliever <b>Lucas Sims</b>. The Sox went 3-for-17 with runners in scoring position. </p><p>"We came out hot and kind of cooled off a little bit there," Benintendi said. </p><h3><b>Measuring Mune’s moonshot</b></h3><p><b>Munetaka Murakami</b>’s Statcast-projected 431-foot grand slam sure felt like a lowball estimate in the Sox clubhouse the morning after the rookie slugger’s seventh-inning rocket cleared the batter’s eye in center field <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox/2026/04/17/white-sox-seranthony-dominguez-anthony-kay-athletics" target="_blank" ><u>to seal Friday’s 9-2 win</u></a>.</p><p>“I got more than 431. I don't know who's doing that calculation, but that ball was touched right there,” said Venable, who categorized it as “a majestic blast.”</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" > <div class="TweetUrl"> <blockquote class="twitter-tweet"><p lang="en" dir="ltr">114.1 MPH<br>OVER the batter's eye<br><br>Munetaka Murakami's first MLB grand slam was a sight to behold! <a href="https://t.co/wFgHwqsLAg">https://t.co/wFgHwqsLAg</a> <a href="https://t.co/YFlLGxwiCB">pic.twitter.com/YFlLGxwiCB</a></p>— MLB (@MLB) <a href="https://twitter.com/MLB/status/2045352938231521432?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">April 18, 2026</a></blockquote> <script async src="https://platform.twitter.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script> </div> </div> </div></div><p>A similar moonshot at Sutter Health Park last summer by Tigers outfielder <b>Riley Greene</b> was clocked at 471 feet.</p><p>From the Sox’ dugout, starter <b>Davis Martin</b> thought <b>Denzel Clarke</b>’s leisurely strides indicated the A’s center fielder had a beat on the 114-mph laser that Murakami cranked off a 98-mph fastball from <b>Elvis Alvarado</b>.</p><p>Then Davis’ jaw dropped.</p><p>“I looked at our pitching coach [<b>Zach Bove</b>] like, ‘Oh my gosh,’” Martin said. “Guy’s got stupid juice.”</p><h3><b>Acuna’s growing pains</b></h3><p><b>Luisangel Acuna</b> snapped an 0-for-21 skid at the plate with a single and followed up with an RBI double for his first extra-base hit in a Sox uniform during their offensive onslaught Friday on a night that encapsulated the 24-year-old’s potential upside and early struggles.</p><p>Acuna, who has learned center field on the job since arriving from the Mets in the <b>Luis Robert Jr.</b> trade, also lost a fly ball in the lights that bounced for a ground-rule double. But he gamely tracked down a few screaming liners and swiped his fifth bag of the season.</p><p>“He's been grinding, like so many of these guys have, and he's working so hard pre-game to get his swing right, to put himself in a good position out there. To get rewarded is great, and just really nice for him, nice for us,” Venable said. “He's a good player and he can hit.”</p><p>Acuna has a paltry .478 OPS compared to .751 for Robert, who <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox/2026/04/18/luis-robert-jr-new-york-mets-chicago-white-sox-mlb-all-star" >hit a double in his return to Chicago on Friday</a> against the Cubs.</p><h3><b>Roster shuffle</b></h3><p>The Sox claimed journeyman right-hander <b>Osvaldo Bido</b> off waivers from the Braves and transferred <b>Prelander Berroa</b> from the 15-day injured list to the 60-day IL in <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox/2026/02/11/erick-fedde-white-sox-return-prelander-berroa" target="_blank" ><u>his recovery from Tommy John surgery</u></a>.</p><p>Bido, 30, joins his fourth team with a 5.13 ERA over 64 career games (28 starts) with 185 strikeouts in 203 ⅔ innings. He gave up seven runs in six relief appearances before being designated for assignment by Atlanta.</p><p>Meanwhile, the Astros claimed outfielder <b>Dustin Harris</b>, whom the Sox DFA’d last week.</p>

entries.title: Man sought after attempted sexual assault on CTA train in Austin
entries.summary: <p>Chicago police are searching for a man who allegedly tried sexually assaulting a woman on a CTA train Saturday in Austin.</p><p>The woman was traveling west on a Blue Line train between the Cicero and Austin stops when the man, who was exposing himself and making sexual comments, approached her, Chicago police said.</p><p>He then attacked her and tried to sexually assault her before fleeing from the train at the Austin stop, police said.</p><p>Police described him as a Black man in his 40s, medium build with short black hair and a full beard. He was wearing a black, unzipped jacket, white t-shirt, dark jeans with red and blue bandanas hanging from the back pockets and white gym shoes.</p><p>Anyone with information is asked to contact Area 4 detectives at (312) 746-8251. Anonymous tips can be submitted at <a class="Link" href="http://cpdtip.com" target="_blank" ><u>cpdtip.com</u></a>.</p>
